entries_new.name: Umm Alhoul Free Zone
entries_new.laws: Disputes fall under the Qatar International Court and Dispute Resolution Centre
entries_new.story: Umm Alhoul Free Zone is a free zone in Qatar. It lies beside Hamad Port and covers 3,000 hectares under Qatar's free zone regime, run by the Qatar Free Zones Authority created in 2018; the Qatar International Court and Dispute Resolution Centre extended its jurisdiction to firms in the authority's zones. Under the Revised Kyoto Convention, a free zone is part of a country's territory where goods brought in are generally treated as outside the customs territory for import duties and taxes.

entries_new.name: Qatar Financial Centre
entries_new.laws: Legal system based on English common law; Civil and Commercial Court and Regulatory Tribunal of the Qatar International Court and Dispute Resolution Centre
entries_new.story: Qatar Financial Centre is a business and financial centre with its own legal system in Doha, Qatar. Set up in March 2005, its legal system is based on English common law, unlike the civil and Sharia system of the rest of Qatar; the Qatar International Court and Dispute Resolution Centre gives it a Civil and Commercial Court and a Regulatory Tribunal. Wikipedia compares its common-law system to those of the Dubai International Financial Centre, the Abu Dhabi Global Market and the Astana International Financial Centre.
